methods.label: Find the students who must sit at the ends
methods.explanation:
Label the students \(A,B,C,D\) in their original left-to-right order. The pairs \(AB,BC,CD\) may no longer sit together, regardless of which member of a pair sits on the left.

Student \(B\) cannot sit next to \(A\) or \(C\), so \(B\)'s only possible neighbor is \(D\). An interior seat has two different neighbors, so \(B\) must sit at an end. Similarly, \(C\)'s only possible neighbor is \(A\), so \(C\) must occupy the other end.

If \(C\) sits at the left end, \(A\) must sit next to \(C\), and \(D\) must sit next to \(B\). This forces the order
\[
C,A,D,B.
\]
If \(B\) sits at the left end, the same restrictions force
\[
B,D,A,C.
\]
Both orders use only the neighbor pairs \(AC,AD,BD\), all of which are allowed. Every valid arrangement must have \(B\) and \(C\) at opposite ends, and each choice of their ends forces exactly one order. Thus there are exactly \(\boxed{2}\) rearrangements, choice \(\text{A}\).
methods.levelReason: Forced neighbors and endpoint reasoning give an exhaustive count using elementary logic. No permutation formula or graph theorem is needed.
